set.name: Signal
set.mechanism: A blip on the night pitch: a dark instrument field, wide tracked capitals set like scoreboard fine print, and exactly one lit green mark.
set.expression_move: The signal-green blip is the only saturated colour anywhere.
set.differs_by: The competitor shelf is community-forum red and unstyled Arial; Signal reads as an instrument — dark, quiet, one lit mark — not as a website theme.

logo.concept: The pitch seen from above at night: the ring, the halfway line, and one lit dot — the player worth your time.

misuse.label: The blip never sits on the centerline — the player is found off it
Never fill the pitch: the mark is a line, not a surface

rationale.claim: The product is a night-shift data instrument: dark ground with one warm-lit mark matches a companion window read at night beside Football Manager.
Green marks 'found value' in this brand; it doubles as the best-fit tier, so brand accent and product semantics point the same way.
Competitor primaries measured: geniescout.com unstyled #0000ee on Arial, fmscout.com #e3042e on Helvetica — the dark/cool region with a green accent is empty on the shelf.

palette.name: Signal
palette.direction: Night-slate ground with one signal-green blip.

brand.name: Night Slate
brand.usage: dark ground, app icon, print covers

brand.name: Signal Green
brand.usage: the blip; highlights and the best-fit score on dark grounds

set.name: Kickoff
set.mechanism: Chalk lines on turf: a saturated pitch-green ground, condensed wide-shouting capitals in chalk, and one corner-flag yellow.
set.expression_move: The green ground itself is the loud part — type and mark stay plain.
set.differs_by: Forum red and badge-and-crest club identity are the category habit; Kickoff borrows the pitch instead — line and turf, no crest.

logo.concept: The corner flag: the one piece of kit that exists in every football ground and nowhere else — a line, not a crest.

defaults_used.why: Chalk #f4f1e6 is a line-white from the turf board, used as paper only; the set's working ground is turf green, not a cream field. Kept because the document side of the pitch needs a non-white paper.

The corner flag is football-specific furniture absent from the competitor shelf (forum red + badges), keeps a second reading as a plain triangle at 16 px, and names what the product is for without becoming a club crest.

rationale.claim: Corner flag over crest: football clubs own crests, a companion tool should borrow the game's neutral furniture instead of imitating a club badge.
Green + yellow is a well-rated pairing direction; the green is the ground (large, quiet chroma) and yellow stays small, so the accent does not fight it.
Condensed display is the sports-sector code, which is exactly what this set wants — it is declared as a deliberate fit, and Sofia Sans Condensed is not the usual Anton/Barlow Condensed shelf.

palette.name: Kickoff
palette.direction: Turf green ground, chalk white, one corner-flag yellow.

set.name: Ledger
set.mechanism: The scouting report: slab capitals on paper, an administrative sans for the small print, scores typed in typewriter mono — and one red stamp square.
set.expression_move: The red stamp square is the only saturated mark; everything else is ink on paper.
set.differs_by: Where the category is dark tool chrome or forum red, the Ledger reads like a printed official report — authority from paper, not from darkness.

logo.concept: The name written into the report, closed with one stamped square — the grade at the end of the line.

defaults_used.why: The scouting report was literally a paper document in this product's history; the paper is low-chroma, the ink is slate, and the accent is a stamp — the set is document, not the cream+terracotta+gold cluster.
Stamp red #bf3a2b is a grade stamp drawn as a 30-unit square once per lockup; it never fills a surface or a band, so it carries the stamp's function rather than the terracotta-clay role.

rationale.claim: Scouting predates software: the scouting report was paper with a typed rating. The set keeps that document's structure — slab name, administrative small print, typewriter figures.
Light ground is the deliberate opposite of the sector's dark-tool default; it stays legible on the desktop next to Football Manager's dark UI because it is low-chroma paper, not white.
Courier Prime gives figures a typed-in, archive feel; monospaced faces are tabular by construction, so the numbers gate is met without a feature.

palette.direction: Ink on report paper, one red stamp.
